name: Texas
summary: Statutes and Constitution: statutes.capitol.texas.gov is now an Angular app that gives the fetch tool an empty shell. The chapter files behind it, at tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/{CODE}/htm/{CODE}.{chapter}.htm, are constructible from any Texas citation and readable by both the fetch tool and fetch_doc.py; official per-code bulk zips and PDFs also exist. Court rules (TRCP, TRAP, TRE, TDRPC) are long PDFs on txcourts.gov that the fetch tool truncates (corpus candidates). Case law: search.txcourts.gov (TAMES: all court of appeals and CCA opinions, dockets, petition dispositions) is closed by robots.txt (Disallow: /); Supreme Court opinions and weekly orders lists (Oct. 2014 on) and Business Court opinions (2024 on, public-domain cites like 2026 Tex. Bus. 72) are on www.txcourts.gov/media; Justia is the only allowed route to court of appeals and CCA opinion text. Admin Code: the SOS viewer is a JavaScript app with no readable text; Cornell LII is the working fallback; Texas Register issue PDFs are on sos.state.tx.us.

citation_map.notes: Statute citations: Bluebook 'Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code Ann. § 16.003 (West 20xx)'; Texas Greenbook (Texas Rules of Form) drops 'Ann.' and the publisher. Every Texas code section number is {chapter}.{section-within-chapter}, so the chapter is the part before the first dot (§ 16.003 → ch. 16; § 552.325 → ch. 552; art. 38.23 → ch. 38; § 2001.038 → ch. 2001; CCP chapters can carry letters: ch. 2A). The Code of Criminal Procedure uses 'art.' not '§'; it was partly recodified effective Jan. 1, 2025 (Acts 2023, H.B. 4504), so pre-2025 article numbers in older opinions may not exist in the current chapter file. 'Prob. Code' (PB) is repealed (replaced by the Estates Code, 2014) — the site no longer lists it in StatuteCodes.json; treat a Probate Code cite as historical. Guard against other states: bare 'Penal Code', 'Government Code', 'Family Code', 'Probate Code', 'Insurance Code', 'Labor Code', 'Education Code', 'Water Code', 'Property Code' route here ONLY with a 'Tex.'/'Texas' prefix — California has Penal Code § 187 and dotted sections like Penal Code § 12022.53, and 'Code of Civil Procedure § 425.16' is California, not Texas. Prose forms without 'Texas' route here only for Texas-unique code names (Civil Practice and Remedies, Code of Criminal Procedure, Business Organizations, Parks and Wildlife, Special District Local Laws, Alcoholic Beverage, Occupations, Human Resources, Business and Commerce, Estates). Bare 'CCP' is ambiguous (California Code of Civil Procedure) and is not routed. A range '§§ 16.003-.004' or '§§ 16.003–16.004' is a span: take the first section only (the regex stops at the hyphen). Bare 'Rule 91a' / 'Rule 47.7' route here only in a Texas context; 'TRE'/'TRAP'/'TRCP' acronyms are Texas-specific. Case citations: Texas cites carry the subsequent-history parenthetical inside the court/date parenthetical. Civil (Sept. 1, 1997 onward, petition for review to the Supreme Court): 'pet. denied', 'pet. granted', 'pet. dism'd', 'pet. dism'd w.o.j.', 'pet. abated', 'pet. filed', 'no pet.' (time expired, none filed), 'no pet. h.' (no history yet). Civil before Sept. 1, 1997 (application for writ of error): 'writ ref'd' (= Supreme Court precedent), 'writ ref'd n.r.e.', 'writ denied', 'writ dism'd w.o.j.', 'writ dism'd by agr.', 'no writ'. Criminal (petition for discretionary review to the Court of Criminal Appeals): 'pet. ref'd', 'pet. granted', 'pet. dism'd', 'untimely pet.', 'no pet.'; 'PDR' is a docket term, not a citation form. Civil petition history → tx-subsequent-scotx-orders (weekly orders lists name the COA docket); criminal 'pet. ref'd' is published only in TAMES (blocked) — cite it as reported, unconfirmed. Courts of appeals: 'Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.]', '[14th Dist.]', 'Tex. App.—Dallas', 'Tex. App.—Austin', 'Tex. App.—San Antonio', 'Tex. App.—Fort Worth', 'Tex. App.—Amarillo', 'Tex. App.—El Paso', 'Tex. App.—Beaumont', 'Tex. App.—Waco', 'Tex. App.—Eastland', 'Tex. App.—Tyler', 'Tex. App.—Texarkana', 'Tex. App.—Corpus Christi–Edinburg' (formerly 'Corpus Christi'); the Fifteenth Court of Appeals (statewide, from Sept. 1, 2024) is cited 'Tex. App.—15th Dist.' (form per orders lists; Greenbook form unverified). COA docket NN-YY-NNNNN-CV/CR: the first two digits are the district (01-15). Unpublished/memorandum opinions: civil memorandum opinions are precedential (TRAP 47.7(b)); criminal opinions marked 'do not publish' / 'not designated for publication' have no precedential value (TRAP 47.7(a)). Supreme Court docket 'No. YY-NNNN' collides with many courts' docket shapes — route only with a '(Tex.' parenthetical. Business Court cites are public-domain ('2026 Tex. Bus. 72 (8th Div.)'), paragraph-pinpointed. The Supreme Court and CCA have no vendor-neutral citation. CourtListener ids (tex, texcrimapp, texapp, texreview) are from memory and unverified; no id known for the Business Court.

sources.title: Texas Constitution and Statutes — chapter files (tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources)
sources.official_status_evidence: No official/unofficial or authentication statement found on the site's information panel or in the app text (statutes.capitol.texas.gov); Texas has no UELMA authentication statement on these files.
sources.coverage: All Texas codes, Vernon's Civil Statutes (CV), Auxiliary Water Laws (WL), uncodified Insurance Code (I1), and the Constitution; one HTML/PDF/DOCX file per chapter; historical versions 2004 onward via the 'Statutes by Date' API.

access.pattern_rules: CODE = two-letter key from law_aliases (CP, PE, CR, GV, FA, BC, BO, …; list at https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/assets/StatuteCodes.json). chapter = the part of the section number before the first dot, unpadded, letters kept (16.003 → CP.16; 19.02 → PE.19; art. 38.23 → CR.38; 552.325 → GV.552; 2001.038 → GV.2001; CR.2A exists). Sections are anchored <a name="16.003"> on the chapter page (the fetch tool ignores the #fragment; search the page for 'Sec. 16.003.' or 'Art. 38.23.'). Same file as PDF: /resources/{CODE}/pdf/{CODE}.{chapter}.pdf; Word: /resources/{CODE}/word/{CODE}.{chapter}.docx. There are NO per-section files for statutes (/CP/htm/CP.16/16.003.htm → 404). Hierarchy (title/subtitle/subchapter) is printed at the top of each chapter file — use it to build tx-statutes-justia URLs.

automation.notes: The fetch tool reads the whole of small and medium chapters (CP.16, 55K chars; PE.19). Large chapters are cut off and offset does NOT reach the rest: GV.552 (346K chars by script) — WebFetch reported only ~103K chars, ending at § 552.113; offset=100000 returned a fragment, § 552.325 NOT PRESENT. Use fetch_doc.py for any chapter over ~90K chars (e.g. GV.552, TX.151 434K, HS.481 295K, FA.153 215K, CR.38 155K), or the chapter PDF.

currency.where: Not on chapter files. Site-wide message from https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/api/GetProperty/StatutesCurrentMsg (shown in the app's Site Information panel)
currency.observed: current through the 89th 2nd Called Legislative Session, 2025

hazards: statutes.capitol.texas.gov (the address everyone cites, incl. old /Docs/CP/htm/CP.16.htm links) is a JavaScript app: the fetch tool and fetch_doc.py get only a code list. Rewrite to tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/… instead.
large chapter files exceed the fetch tool's window and offsets do not recover the tail (GV.552 § 552.325 unreachable) — use fetch_doc.py
#section anchors are ignored by the fetch tool
no currency line in the files themselves
CCP recodification (eff. 1/1/2025) moved many articles; old article numbers may be absent
text includes future-effective versions: some sections appear twice ('Text of section effective on …') — check effective-date notes

probe.expect: Except as provided by Sections 16.010, 16.0031, and 16.0045, a

verification.evidence: WebFetch: § 16.003 YES 'Except as provided by Sections 16.010, 16.0031, and 16.0045, a'; complete through § 16.073. Second code: PE.19 § 19.02(b) YES 'A person commits an offense if the person: (1) intentionally'. fetch_doc.py verify OK on both; CR.38 art. 38.23 and GV.552 § 552.325 found by script grep. Large-chapter test: GV.552 § 552.325 NOT PRESENT in WebFetch even with offset.

sources.notes: Bulk: per-code zips at https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/Zips/{CODE}.htm.zip (also .pdf.zip, .doc.zip; CP.htm.zip 655,256 bytes, HTTP 200) and whole-code PDFs at /resources/SDocs/{CODENAME}.pdf (e.g. CIVILPRACTICEANDREMEDIESCODE.pdf, 1.8 MB) — list in https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/assets/StatuteCodeDownloads.json (paths there are relative to /resources). Note /Zips/… without /resources → 404. API base https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/api/ (GetProperty/{name}, StatutesByDate/GetCodes/{yyyy-mm-dd}, DocViewer/GetDocument/…).

sources.title: Supreme Court of Texas — Orders & Opinions pages and opinion PDFs (txcourts.gov)
sources.official_status_evidence: Slip opinions with slip pagination; reported versions appear in S.W.3d (West).
sources.coverage: One page per order/opinion release day from Oct. 2014 to date (year pages 2014-2026; /2013/ and earlier → 404). Each page lists orders on causes, petitions granted/denied, mandamus and habeas orders, and links each opinion, concurrence and dissent as a PDF.

access.pattern_rules: month = full lower-case month name; D unpadded (may-29-2026). Release dates are irregular (usually Fridays, plus extra days): take them from the year page /supreme/orders-opinions/{YYYY}/. Opinion PDFs: /media/{id}/{docket without hyphen}{suffix}.pdf (240205.pdf; 240205c.pdf concurring; 240286d.pdf dissent) — the media id is not derivable; take it from the day page. Older pages may keep the hyphen (12-0657c1.pdf).
access.navigation: year page → release-day page → 'opinion of the Court' / 'concurring opinion' link (/media/…pdf). Print-friendly orders PDF on each day page (supreme-court-of-texas-orders-MM-DD-YYYY.pdf).

sources.title: Supreme Court of Texas weekly orders — petitions for review granted/denied
sources.official_status_evidence: The Court's own orders lists ('Orders Pronounced'), also as print-friendly PDF.
sources.coverage: Oct. 2014 to date. Every petition entry gives SC docket, parties, county, court of appeals district and the COA docket, reporter cite and judgment date, e.g. '(05-23-00190-CV, ___ SW3d ___, 08-21-24)'. Also mandamus, habeas, rehearing dispositions.

access.pattern_rules: No search. Petition for review must be filed within 45 days of the COA judgment (TRAP 53.7) and is usually decided 3-12 months later: scan the release-day pages after the COA judgment date for the COA docket number (NN-YY-NNNNN-CV) — it appears verbatim on the page. WebSearch with the quoted COA docket and site:txcourts.gov did not find it (2026-10-16 test returned unrelated pages).
access.navigation: year page → each release-day page after the COA judgment → search page text for the COA docket under 'PETITIONS FOR REVIEW ARE DENIED' / 'GRANTED'

automation.notes: A script could crawl the ~60 day pages per year once and index COA docket → disposition (see script_candidates).

hazards: no docket search; linear scan of day pages
denials before Oct. 2014 not on txcourts.gov
criminal cases never appear here (CCA handles PDRs)

script_candidates.why: Static chapter files with name="{section}" anchors at a URL built from the citation; per-code zips (/resources/Zips/{CODE}.htm.zip) give the whole code in one download; API https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/api/ exposes GetProperty/StatutesCurrentMsg (currency) and StatutesByDate/* (versions back to 2004).

Release-day pages are plain HTML with every petition entry carrying the COA docket; a crawler over 2014-2026 (~60 pages/year) can build COA docket → Supreme Court docket + disposition + date, turning civil 'pet. denied/granted' into a lookup.
One listing page holds every opinion with its public-domain cite, cause number, judge, date and PDF link — trivially parsed into 'YYYY Tex. Bus. N' → PDF.
